subtitle: How a Yadava minister tried to bind a kingdom into a single book of duty

panels.shot: low-angle three-quarter view, wide interior of a lamplit manuscript hall
panels.action: Hemadri Pandit stands at a long wooden desk in Devagiri, palm-leaf bundles rising around him like walls, his hand resting on a thick manuscript while courtiers and scribes blur in the shadowed background.

dialogue.text: In the Yadava age of Devagiri, Hemadri Pandit dared to gather vows, gifts, law, medicine and royal memory into one vast book of duty—and hoped a kingdom could live inside its leaves.

i18n.hi: देवगिरी के यादव युग में हेमाद्रि पंडित ने हिम्मत की — व्रत, दान, कानून, चिकित्सा और राजस्मृति सबको एक विशाल धर्म‑पुस्तक में समेटने की, मानो पूरा राज्य उसी के पन्नों में बस सके।

panels.shot: epic bird’s-eye view over the plateau fortress and city below
panels.action: From high above Devagiri, stone walls crown a rocky hill while at its base markets, temples and dusty roads spread out; in a balcony recess, Hemadri Pandit watches the bustle with a thoughtful, measuring gaze.

dialogue.text: Mid-13th century Deccan. The Yadava kings rule from Devagiri, a hill of stone above a plain of trade. Here, a minister named Hemadri Pandit studies not only people, but the rules that claim to bind them.

i18n.hi: तेरहवीं सदी का मध्य, दक्खन। यादव राजा पत्थर की पहाड़ी देवगिरी से राज करते हैं, नीचे फैला व्यापार‑मैदान। यहीं मंत्री हेमाद्रि पंडित सिर्फ लोगों को नहीं, उन्हें बाँधने वाले नियमों को भी पढ़ता है।

panels.shot: medium interior shot, candlelit study with scrolls and icons
panels.action: In a quiet chamber, Hemadri sits cross-legged before a low desk, palm-leaf manuscripts stacked on either side, a small image of a deity behind him; he leans forward, reading an older dharmashastra text by lamplight.

dialogue.text: Hemadri is a pandit and a minister. His world is filled with old dharmashastra texts—Manu, Yajnavalkya, countless commentaries—each prescribing duties, vows, gifts, penances. But they lie scattered, hard to wield in daily rule.

i18n.hi: हेमाद्रि पंडित भी है, मंत्री भी। उसका संसार पुरानी धर्मशास्त्र पुस्तकों से भरा है — मनु, याज्ञवल्क्य, असंख्य टीकाएँ — जो व्रत, दान, प्रायश्चित्त, कर्तव्य सब बताते हैं। पर ये सब बिखरे पड़े हैं, रोज़मर्रा के राजकाज में पकड़ से बाहर।

panels.shot: close-up on Hemadri’s face lit by the lamp, eyes intent
panels.action: Hemadri’s lined face is framed in shadow and flame, his eyes narrowed in concentration as his finger traces a line on a brittle palm leaf, several different manuscripts open around him.

dialogue.text: He sees the gap: kings, priests, donors, pilgrims all ask, what is the right act here and now? The answers are buried across ages. Hemadri decides to stitch them together—into one Chaturvarga Chintamani, a ‘jewel of the four aims of life’.

i18n.hi: उसे खाई दिखती है: राजा, पुरोहित, दाता, तीर्थयात्री सब पूछते हैं, अभी‑यहीं सही काम क्या है? जवाब युगों में बिखरे हैं। हेमाद्रि ठानता है उन्हें सिलने की — एक चतुर्वर्ग चिंतामणि में, ‘जीवन के चार पुरुषार्थों का रत्न’।

panels.shot: wide interior shot of a court hall with scribes at work
panels.action: In the Yadava royal court, Hemadri stands before seated ministers and scribes, unrolling a long palm-leaf bundle while young scribes sit with styluses poised; a faint outline of King Mahadeva on a raised seat is visible in the background.

dialogue.speaker: hemadri_pandit
dialogue.text: We will gather vows, gifts and expiations, sire—so no man must grope in doubt.

i18n.hi: हम सारे व्रत, दान और प्रायश्चित्त जुटाएँगे, महाराज — ताकि कोई अँधेरे में टटोलता न रहे।

panels.shot: medium shot of Hemadri dictating, scribes in foreground
panels.action: Hemadri sits upright on a mat, dictating steadily while a row of scribes scratch letters into palm leaves, piles of labeled bundles—‘vows’, ‘gifts’, ‘penances’—growing around them.

dialogue.text: Hemadri arranges his Chaturvarga Chintamani into sections—on observances and vows, on gifts of land and wealth, on expiation, on liberation. He does not erase the older voices; he quotes them line by line, preserving their words.

i18n.hi: हेमाद्रि अपना चतुर्वर्ग चिंतामणि खंडों में सजाता है — नियम‑अनुष्ठान और व्रत, भूमि और धनदान, प्रायश्चित्त, मोक्ष। वह पुरानी आवाज़ें नहीं मिटाता; उन्हें पंक्ति‑दर‑पंक्ति उद्धृत करता है, उनके शब्द बचाकर।

panels.shot: over-the-shoulder shot of a manuscript leaf
panels.action: Seen over Hemadri’s shoulder, a palm-leaf page shows neat lines while in the margins tiny notches separate quotations; more piles of ancient manuscripts lie open beside his working copy.

dialogue.text: P.V. Kane, centuries later, will trace countless lost works through these quotations. A Yadava minister, seeking order for his king, unwittingly becomes the archivist of India’s older dharmashastra memory.

i18n.hi: सदियों बाद पी.वी. काणे इन्हीं उद्धरणों से अनगिनत खोई रचनाएँ पहचानेंगे। अपने राजा के लिए व्यवस्था खोजता यादव मंत्री अनजाने में भारत के प्राचीन धर्मशास्त्र का अभिलेखपाल बन जाता है।

panels.shot: medium shot in a temple courtyard, donors and priests present
panels.action: In a sunlit temple courtyard, a land donor stands with folded hands before a priest; Hemadri observes quietly, holding a bound palm-leaf book, as a scribe marks something on a flat board beside them.

dialogue.text: Gifts to temples, lands for brahmanas, vows taken by traders and widows—all pass through the language of dharma. Hemadri’s manual offers forms, precedents, promises of merit. It is law, ritual and royal policy braided together.

i18n.hi: मंदिरों को दान, ब्राह्मणों की भूमि, व्यापारियों और विधवाओं के व्रत — सब धर्म की भाषा से होकर गुजरते हैं। हेमाद्रि की पुस्तिका में रूप, मिसालें, पुण्य के वादे हैं। यह कानून, अनुष्ठान और राजनीति तीनों का गुंथा हुआ धागा है।

panels.shot: dramatic low-angle shot in the court, Hemadri reciting genealogy
panels.action: In the royal hall, Hemadri, standing with a scroll, recites before nobles as musicians and bards listen; a carved panel behind him shows Yadava kings in relief, evoking the dynasty’s imagined lineage.

dialogue.text: Within his dharma-book, Hemadri praises his patrons. He recounts Yadava genealogy, their victories, their gifts as if cast in legend. These passages are panegyrics, not neutral chronicle—a minister’s tribute woven into a manual of duty.

i18n.hi: अपने धर्म‑ग्रंथ के भीतर हेमाद्रि अपने संरक्षकों की स्तुति करता है। वह यादव वंशावली, विजय और दान को मानो कथा‑काव्य की तरह सुनाता है। ये अंश प्रशस्ति हैं, सीधी इतिहास‑कथा नहीं — मंत्री की भक्ति, जो कर्तव्य‑ग्रंथ में बुनी गई है।

panels.shot: close-up of a courtier whispering to another, Hemadri in background
panels.action: Two courtiers lean toward each other, murmuring, as Hemadri continues to read, his back to them; one gestures subtly toward the ornate genealogy reliefs.

dialogue.text: Later readers will mine these laudatory lines for Yadava history, but the record is bent by praise. Hemadri’s book shows not merely what happened, but how a court wished to remember itself.

i18n.hi: आने वाले पाठक इन्हीं प्रशंसा‑पंक्तियों से यादव इतिहास खोदेंगे, पर यह दास्तान प्रशंसा से टेढ़ी है। हेमाद्रि की किताब सिर्फ ‘क्या हुआ’ नहीं दिखाती, यह भी दिखाती है कि दरबार खुद को कैसे याद रखना चाहता था।

panels.shot: medium shot inside a quieter inner room, Hemadri with a physician
panels.action: In a smaller chamber lined with medical texts, Hemadri confers with an older physician, an open copy of Vagbhata’s Ashtangahridayam between them; he holds a fresh palm leaf, ready to annotate.

dialogue.text: Hemadri’s hunger for system does not end with ritual. He turns to medicine, composing his Ayurveda Rasayan, a commentary on Vagbhata’s Ashtangahridayam. Here too, he links older knowledge to his own day.

i18n.hi: हेमाद्रि की व्यवस्था की भूख केवल अनुष्ठान तक नहीं रुकती। वह चिकित्सा की ओर मुड़ता है और आयुर्वेद रसायन रचता है — वाग्भट के अष्टाङ्गहृदय पर टीका। यहाँ भी वह पुराने ज्ञान को अपने समय से जोड़ता है।

panels.shot: over-the-shoulder shot of a medical diagram or verse
panels.action: Over Hemadri’s shoulder we glimpse a palm leaf inscribed with verses on humors and treatments, neat annotations filling the margins as his stylus hovers over a line.

dialogue.text: In the Rasayan, Hemadri extends the classical medical tradition, glossing ailments, therapies, and the physician’s conduct. Law, ritual and healing all pass under his pen, as if the same idea of order ran through body and kingdom.

i18n.hi: रसायन में हेमाद्रि आयुर्वेद की परंपरा बढ़ाता है — रोग, उपचार और वैद्य के आचरण पर व्याख्या करता है। कानून, अनुष्ठान और चिकित्सा — सब उसकी कलम से गुजरते हैं, मानो वही एक व्यवस्था शरीर और राज्य दोनों में बह रही हो।

panels.shot: medium interior shot, Hemadri with visiting scholars and students
panels.action: Hemadri sits at the head of a low platform while younger students and visiting scholars surround him, some holding palm-leaf bundles; he gestures toward a stack labeled and tied, as if explaining how they are arranged.

dialogue.speaker: hemadri_pandit
dialogue.text: Do not trust memory alone. Place each vow, each gift, where it can be found.

i18n.hi: केवल स्मृति पर मत टिको। हर व्रत, हर दान को ऐसी जगह लिखो जहाँ वह फिर मिल सके।

panels.shot: wide night-time shot of Devagiri’s ramparts under stars
panels.action: Under a starry sky, the silhouette of Devagiri’s ramparts looms over the dark plain; within a lit window slit, Hemadri’s figure is just visible bending over his desk, the city sleeping below.

dialogue.text: He serves under Mahadeva and into the early reign of Ramachandra. Beyond the walls, rival powers move—the Kakatiyas, the Delhi sultans—but Hemadri’s battles are with confusion, contradiction, forgotten precedent.

i18n.hi: वह महादेव के अधीन और रामचंद्र के आरंभिक शासन तक सेवा करता है। दीवारों के बाहर प्रतिद्वंदी ताकतें उठती हैं — काकतीय, दिल्ली के सुलतान — पर हेमाद्रि की लड़ाइयाँ उलझन, विरोध, भूले‑बिसरे उदाहरणों से हैं।

panels.shot: medium shot of storytellers later, pointing to a script scroll
panels.action: Generations later, in a village setting, two storytellers sit by a lamp; one points proudly to a scroll with bold script as a child listens, while a faint, idealised image of Hemadri appears in the background like a memory.

dialogue.text: Later tradition will credit Hemadri with creating or standardising the Modi script. It is a good story for a learned minister, but no firm 13th-century evidence supports it; the earliest dated Modi records belong to much later days.

i18n.hi: बाद की परंपरा हेमाद्रि को मोडी लिपि का जनक या नियंत्रक बताएगी। विद्वान मंत्री के लिए यह अच्छी कहानी है, पर तेरहवीं सदी का ठोस सबूत नहीं; मोडी के सबसे पुराने दिनांकित अभिलेख बहुत बाद के हैं।

panels.shot: close-up of a cracked but legible Chaturvarga Chintamani leaf centuries later
panels.action: A centuries-old palm-leaf folio of Chaturvarga Chintamani lies on a wooden table, edges cracked yet letters sharp; a modern researcher’s hand, unseen above, turns the page with care.

dialogue.text: What survives securely is his writing. P.V. Kane, in the twentieth century, will sit with such leaves, reconstructing dharmashastra history through Hemadri’s quotations and arrangements, hearing across time the mind of a Yadava minister at work.

i18n.hi: जो ठोस रूप से बचा है, वह उसकी लेखनी है। बीसवीं सदी में पी.वी. काणे इन्हीं पन्नों पर झुककर हेमाद्रि के उद्धरणों और संयोजन से धर्मशास्त्र‑इतिहास फिर गढ़ेंगे, समय के पार एक यादव मंत्री का मन काम करता सुनेंगे।

panels.shot: final wide shot blending Hemadri at his desk with faint outlines of kings and commoners
panels.action: In a layered composition, Hemadri sits writing at his desk while around him, like translucent silhouettes, appear a king granting land, a widow taking a vow, a physician tending a patient, all tethered by invisible lines to his manuscript.

dialogue.text: The Yadava kingdom falls, its walls broken and palaces emptied. Yet Hemadri’s Chaturvarga Chintamani and Ayurveda Rasayan endure, showing how one court imagined right action—reminding us that a state outlives itself in the manuals it leaves behind.

i18n.hi: यादव राज्य गिरता है, दीवारें टूटती हैं, महल सूने हो जाते हैं। पर हेमाद्रि का चतुर्वर्ग चिंतामणि और आयुर्वेद रसायन बने रहते हैं, दिखाते हुए कि एक दरबार ने ‘सही कर्म’ कैसी कल्पना की — याद दिलाते हुए कि राज्य अपने पीछे छोड़ी पुस्तिकाओं में ही सबसे लंबे समय तक जीता रहता है।

subtitle_i18n.en: How a Yadava minister tried to bind a kingdom into a single book of duty
subtitle_i18n.hi: कैसे एक यादव मंत्री ने सारे राजधर्म को एक ही धर्म‑ग्रंथ में बाँधना चाहा
